query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Clean, well-separated semantic categories (email, database, vpn, network) with reasonable distribution; resolution_time can be grouped and compared across these, a highly informative segmentation. Overlaps somewhat with the existing 'category' column but adds interpretable structure.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Distinct, human-interpretable symptom classes (cannot_connect, access_denied, service_down) that plausibly relate to how long incidents take to resolve; good for segmentation, though cannot_connect dominates.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Interpretable system-level categories; useful axis to compare resolution_time. Largely collinear with incident_category (email->email_server etc.), so partially redundant but still a valid segmentation variable.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Excellent EDA variable: scope of impact (individual_user vs enterprise_wide vs remote_access) is external to resolution_time, well-separated, and plausibly associated with how long resolution takes.

per_column.name: is_self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Binary interpretable flag likely strongly associated with resolution_time, but risks partially restating the outcome (self-resolved incidents may be defined by fast/no-agent resolution); still a meaningful comparison group. High NULL rate weakens it.

per_column.name: has_assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary; can compare resolution_time with vs without an agent. Somewhat imbalanced (435/65) but usable as a segmentation.

per_column.name: incident_open_status
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident is still open is entangled with resolution_time itself (open incidents may lack a resolution time); this restates the outcome/state rather than providing an external explanatory axis.

per_column.name: caller_user
per_column.rationale: High-cardinality identifier-like values (individual names); no interpretable, generalizable category structure for comparing resolution_time. Opaque for human understanding of relationships.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely informative, interpretable segmentation axes (scope_indicator, failure_symptom_type, incident_category, affected_system) that let a human explore how resolution_time varies. However informativeness is diluted: incident_category/affected_system are mutually redundant and overlap the existing category column, incident_open_status and partly is_self_resolved restate the outcome/state, and caller_user is an opaque identifier providing no meaningful comparison. A strong but imperfect EDA augmentation.
